newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures spike higher after soft data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures spike higher after soft data.

text.p: U.S. debt futures spiked higher after U.S. economic data that was on the soft side of forecasts and soothed inflation jitters.
July U.S. producer prices fell 0.1 percent overall and in the core rate. Economists on average had expected 0.1-percent gains in each measure.
Retail sales gained 0.6 percent overall versus forecasts for a 0.7-percent gain and rose 0.5 percent excluding autos, matching forecasts.
The data sent September Treasury bond futures soaring, especially after Tuesday's late drop on inflation nerves.
"The decline in the PPI is what got everybody excited," said Kathy Jones, analyst at Prudential Securities. "(But) it's a mystery to me as to why food and energy prices... weren't up in July."
However, she said the data did not alter expectations the the Federal Reserve will stand pat on interest rates at its late-August policymaking meeting.
"Nobody expected them to do anything at this meeting," Jones said. "The expectations are for the next meeting or the meeting after that."
Jones added that the Fed is viewed as focusing on the demand side, which could keep them wary about the economy's strength despite recently benign inflation figures.

Technicals added lift as September T-bonds bounced upward and cleared resistance near Tuesday's peak at 113-10/32, a level that had repelled the contract Tuesday and encouraged some longs to bail out, contributing to the late decline, brokers said.
"That 113-09/32-10/32 is a pivotal area," Jones added. "If we close above that, we'll probably extend the rally back to 114 and change, on a correction."

At 0843 CDT/1343 GMT, September T-bonds rose 24/32 to 113-07/32, 10-year notes gained 13/32 to 109-04/32, muni-bonds gained 18/32 to 119-11/32, December Eurodollars rallied 0.085 to 94.080, and T-bills added 0.100 at 94.800. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
